Thereupon Shatrughna instantly answered saying :-
" What, shalt thou escape me alive? He who has any wit 
does not allow a foe to go free who has come forth of his own 
accord. 
He, who, in his stupidity, suffers a foe to escape, 
perishes. Look long on the world, for, with my whetted shafts, 
I shall despatch thee to Yama's abode, thou the enemy of the 
Three Worlds and of Raghava."

The Death of U.vana

" When others were slain by thee, I was not yet born, but

Then Lavana, beside himself with anger on hearing these

he severed it into a hundred pieces, and the Rakshasa, finding

Thereupon the Rakshasa, thinking Shatrughna to be slain, 
did not enter his house, though tbe opportunity presented 
itself and, seeing him lying on tbe earth, he did not go in search 
of his trident, but, reflecting, " He is dead," he began to collect 
his food. 
Shatrughna, however, regaining his senses, in an instant took 
hold of his weapon and went to his place at the city gate once 
more, amidst tbe acclamations of tbe Rishis ; and he selected a 
celestial, infallible and marvellous arrow that illumined the 
ten regions with its brilliance and resembled lightning in its 
velocity. 
That shaft, smeared with sandal paste of the colour of 
blood, wonderfully plumed, was greatly feared by the leaders of 
the Danavas, the mountains and also the Asuras, and, beholding 
that dreadful weapon, flaming like Time at tbe end of tbe world 
period, all beings were seized with terror. Then Devas, Asuras, 
Gandharvas and troops of Apsaras and tbe whole universe 
trembled and took refuge with the Grandsire of tbe worlds. 
Thereafter the Gods, beside themselves with fear, enquired of 
that Lord of Lords, the Bestower of Grace, tbe Grandsire of the 
Worlds, whether the universe were about to be destrOyed. 
Hearing them speak tbus, Brahma, the Grandsire, addressed 
them in soothiug accents, that restored their serenity, saying :-
" Hear me, 0 Ye Gods, it is in order to destrOy Lavana in 
combat that Shatrughna is armed with that weapon. 0 Fore-
most nf tbe Gods, all are overwhelmed by the power of this 
eternal weapon forged by the primeval God, tbe Creator of tbe 
World. 0 My Children, that ctrulgent shaft which causes such 
terror was fashioned for tbe destruction of the demons, Madhu 
and Kaitabba, by tbe magnanimous God, Vishnu, who alone 
understands it. In reality, it is tbe primeval form of Vishnu 
Himself, therefore go and witness tbe death of the foremost of 
the Raksbasas, Lavana, under the blows of that valiant warrior, 
the younger brother of Rama."

brief.summary_1line: Shatrughna battles the demon Lavana, recovers from a blow, and prepares a terrifying divine arrow of Vishnu to destroy him.

image_candidates.scene_text: Lavana hurls a massive tree at Shatrughna, who slices it into hundreds of pieces with flashing arrows in midair.
Shatrughna lies unconscious after a crushing blow while sages, gods, and celestial beings cry out in alarm from the sky.
Shatrughna raises a blazing celestial arrow that lights the ten directions, making gods and spirits tremble across the universe.

deep.rich_summary: Shatrughna confronts the demon Lavana, refusing to let the Rakshasa escape once he has appeared for battle. Enraged, Lavana attacks with massive trees, hurling them like weapons, but Shatrughna shatters them with his arrows. The demon finally strikes Shatrughna senseless with a tree, prompting cries of alarm from sages, gods, and celestial beings who watch the combat. Mistakenly believing his foe dead, Lavana pauses to gather food rather than finish him. Shatrughna quickly recovers, returns to the city gate, and prepares a terrifying celestial arrow whose radiance shakes the entire universe. Alarmed gods ask Brahma if cosmic destruction is at hand, but he reassures them: the weapon is Vishnu’s primordial power itself, destined to destroy Lavana and end the demon’s tyranny.

highlight_spans.why: Opening challenge establishes the uncompromising warrior ethos and frames the duel as inevitable.
Lavana’s furious reaction—clapping his hands, grinding his teeth, and attacking—captures the emotional escalation into violent combat.
Shatrughna selects the radiant celestial arrow whose brilliance lights the ten directions, marking the mythic turning point of the battle.
Brahma explains the weapon’s origin as a primordial manifestation of Vishnu created to destroy demons, revealing the cosmic scale behind the duel.

top_scenes.scene_text: Lavana hurls enormous trees like missiles while Shatrughna stands firm, slicing them apart midair with flashing arrows.
The moment Shatrughna raises the blazing celestial arrow that illuminates all ten directions as gods and spirits tremble in the sky.
In the heavens, frightened gods gather before Brahma as the universe shakes from the power of the weapon about to strike Lavana.
